title: A lack of professional AI guidelines leads to feelings of "AI shame," a new study finds
tldr: A new study finds professionals (including journalists and academics) hide their AI use out of shame because organizations lack clear guidelines. It reveals a governance gap that communicators need to close.
why_fresh: new research on a behavioral shift
angle: Write about why 'AI shame' is a content-governance failure and how to build permission-based AI guidelines that reduce secrecy.

title: AI Agents Are the New Gatekeepers
tldr: Gini Dietrich argues AI agents are becoming the new intermediaries between brands and audiences—and unlike media, no budget can buy your way in. A provocative reframe of earned visibility.
angle: Explore how PESO and earned media strategy must adapt when AI agents, not humans, decide what surfaces.

title: Dr. Martens Turns to Heritage and Wearers to Tell a New Story Amid Turnaround
tldr: Dr. Martens leans on its heritage and real wearers (user-generated, people-first content) to reboot its brand narrative during a turnaround. A concrete case study in employee/customer-driven storytelling.
angle: Break down how wearer-led storytelling beats polish in a brand turnaround and what content strategists can borrow.

title: The $100 billion comeback of the American tween
tldr: Brands are once again taking tweens seriously as a $100B market, building culture around them like the '90s mall era. A useful look at how a demographic's media and consumption habits reshape marketing.
angle: Write on how tween media-consumption habits are rebuilding brand culture-making—and what it signals for audience strategy.

title: The New Boss at the Chattanooga Times Free Press
tldr: After gutting most staff, new owner Craig Fuller is remaking a legacy paper with drastic changes. A stark case study in local news business models and reputation under new ownership.
angle: Examine what a gutted-then-rebuilt local paper reveals about sustainable media business models.

title: 4 ways communicators can prepare for AI-driven reputation risk
tldr: As AI systems answer questions and make decisions on behalf of brands, communicators must manage trust when humans aren't speaking. Practical framing of an emerging reputation risk.
angle: Write a playbook for managing brand trust when AI—not a human—is the one talking to your public.

title: Startup Spotlight: Marketing vets launch Kompeld to measure if a company's story is actually working
tldr: A new startup aims to measure whether a company's narrative is actually landing—narrative as a measurable asset. Interesting intersection of storytelling and analytics.
angle: Can you actually measure a corporate narrative? Explore what 'story analytics' means for comms teams.

title: The Only Two Types of Content that AI Can Never Make
tldr: Orbit Media argues there are two kinds of content AI can't produce—pointing toward human experience and original research as durable differentiators. A useful human-centered content thesis.
angle: Make the case for the irreplaceable human content moats in an AI-flooded feed.

title: Blogging Statistics 2026: What 1,042 Content Marketers Told Us About What Works
tldr: Fresh survey of over 1,000 content marketers on what actually works in 2026, including AI's impact and evolving formats. Data-rich fuel for content-strategy takes.
angle: Pull the counterintuitive findings from the 2026 data and argue what content teams should stop doing.

title: AI Traffic Conversion Rates: New Research from 97 B2B Websites and 29M visits
tldr: New research finds AI-referred traffic converts differently than search traffic across 97 B2B sites and 29M visits. Concrete data on how AI search is reshaping performance.
angle: Analyze what AI-referral conversion data means for content attribution and where to invest.

title: Condé Nast, Hearst among 300 media execs to push federal 'bad bots' bill on AI scraping
tldr: Over 300 publishing executives are lobbying Congress to curb AI bots scraping their content. A pivotal moment in the media-vs-AI battle over content ownership.
angle: Assess what a coordinated publisher stand against AI scraping means for the future of owned media value.

title: The Rundown: Average CMO tenure has shrunk by over a third in 16 years
tldr: CMO tenure has dropped by more than a third in 16 years amid rising client-side turnover, per a 13,000-marketer survey. Signals instability in marketing leadership and content continuity.
angle: Argue how shrinking CMO tenure sabotages long-term brand narrative and content strategy.

title: Ad of the Day: OpenAI's grandmas put ChatGPT Voice through its paces
tldr: OpenAI's new ad uses grandmas testing ChatGPT Voice—a humanizing, people-first approach to marketing an AI product. A neat craft example of humanity over tech-polish.
angle: Break down why 'grandmas testing AI' works better than product-demo polish for humanizing tech brands.

title: Journalism in the Age of the Quick Take
tldr: Razia Iqbal reflects on how the rush for quick reactions is reshaping journalism and audience attention. A thoughtful media-consumption angle.
angle: Explore how the 'quick take' economy changes how audiences consume and trust content.

title: DesignRush Podcast: HubSpot CMO Kipp Bodnar on AI Search After 140M Lost Visits
tldr: HubSpot's CMO discusses how AI search cost them 140M visits and how they're rethinking content strategy. A candid, concrete case study of content decay in the AI era.
angle: Unpack HubSpot's 140M lost-visits story as a warning about over-reliance on search-optimized content.
